title: Repair ephemeral metric siphon and real-time widget repopulation
creator: Liam Chen
description: High-severity customer reports: intermittent blanks and missing timeseries in Console livepanels during sustained ingest spikes across Hosted and Dedicated tenants. Symptoms include widgets showing "no data" for up to 30m, traces with missing span anchors and disconnected trace-links, and inconsistent metric counts between raw ingest and dashboard aggregates. This ticket implements a safe repair path (snapshot-bridge + WAL rehydration) and UI safeguards to repopulate realtime widgets without causing further write amplification or long stalls.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use load harness to send 3x normal token-rate traffic for 45 minutes to a tenant with high cardinality metrics.
2) Trigger a rolling restart of telemetry-aggregator during peak (simulate k8s drain).
3) Observe livepanel widgets go to 'no data' and metric rollups report lower counts while raw WAL shows accepted writes.
4) Correlate trace IDs to find missing span-anchor events in the span index.
root_cause: A combination of the telemetry shard eviction heuristic and a late KV-cache rotation caused ephemeral in-memory buckets to be dropped during high ingress. When aggregator restarted, WAL replay logic skipped small-window buckets due to an off-by-one watermark calculation. Additionally, the livepanel refresh path assumed eventual consistency and skipped gap-tolerant lookups if upstream shard reported 'healthy'—this prevented automatic rehydration. The result: accepted writes on WAL but incomplete materialization into the queryable aggregates and span index, leaving dashboards blank and trace links broken.
proposed_fix:
1) Implement 'snapshot-bridge' component: on aggregator startup, it will scan WAL and materialized-snapshots to identify skipped buckets and create idempotent rehydration batches.
2) Fix watermark computation (off-by-one) in ingestion preflight so small windows are not ignored.
3) Harden livepanel query path with gap-tolerant fallback queries that surface partial results and queue background backfill jobs instead of returning 'no data'.
4) Add a rate-limited rehydrate worker to avoid write storms and an opt-in fast-path for Dedicated tenants with reserved capacity.
5) Add end-to-end integration tests simulating restarts and high-cardinality spikes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary - console-2025.03): deploy snapshot-bridge and watermark fix to staging and 2 small production tenants for 48h. Enable detailed logging and a metric to count rehydrated buckets. Phase 2: enable gap-tolerant livepanel queries with conservative timeouts for 10% of tenants. Phase 3: increase rollout to 100% and enable Dedicated fast-path. If any customer-facing regression seen, rollback livepanel query change only and keep snapshot-bridge active. Communication: send status update to impacted customers and attach backfill ETA.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard livepanel no-data incidents no longer reproducible under the load harness scenario
Rehydration completes within SLO (95% of skipped buckets processed within 15 minutes for canary tenants)
No more than a 10% increase in write-amplification observed during rehydration on canary tenants
Integration test added to CI that simulates aggregator restart with high ingress and asserts dashboard convergence
